name: Boondi Raita
ingredients: 2 cups thick curd (whisked), 1 cup boondi (soaked in water 5 min, squeezed), 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, ½ tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp sugar, 1 tbsp mint (chopped), 1 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Soak boondi in warm water for 5 minutes to soften. Squeeze gently. STEP 2: In a bowl, whisk curd until smooth. STEP 3: Add soaked boondi, salt, sugar, roasted cumin powder, and red chilli powder. Mix. STEP 4: Garnish with mint and coriander. Chill 10 minutes. Serve cold with biryani or pulao.
tips: The perfect cooling accompaniment. Soaking boondi is crucial — otherwise it stays hard.

name: Masala Dosa
ingredients: FOR BATTER: 2 cups rice, 1 cup urad dal, ½ tsp fenugreek, 1 tsp salt (soak + grind + ferment 8 hours). FOR ALOO MASALA: 4 boiled potatoes (mashed coarsely), 1 onion (chopped), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp urad dal, 1 tsp chana dal, 10 curry leaves, 2 green chillies, ¼ tsp asafoetida, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp coriander, oil for cooking dosa
preparation: STEP 1 (BATTER — DAY BEFORE): Wash and soak rice and urad dal separately for 4 hours. Grind separately to smooth batters. Combine, add salt, and ferment overnight (8 hours). STEP 2 (ALOO MASALA): Heat oil. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add urad dal and chana dal — roast until golden. STEP 3: Add curry leaves, green chillies, asafoetida. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 4: Add onion. Sauté 3 minutes. STEP 5: Add turmeric. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 6: Add mashed potatoes and salt. Mix well with a splash of water. Cook 5 minutes. Add coriander. STEP 7 (DOSA): Heat a flat tawa on medium heat. STEP 8: Pour a ladle of batter. Spread in a circular motion from center outward using the back of the ladle to form a thin large dosa. STEP 9: Drizzle 1 tsp oil around edges. Cook 2-3 minutes until bottom is golden and crisp. STEP 10: Place 2 tbsp aloo masala in the center. Fold dosa over. STEP 11: Serve immediately with sambar and coconut chutney.
tips: Fermentation is what creates the perfect dosa flavour. Cannot be rushed. Tawa temperature must be right — too hot = dosa sticks; too cold = dosa doesn't crisp.

name: Idli Sambar
ingredients: FOR IDLI: 3 cups idli rice, 1 cup urad dal, ½ tsp fenugreek, 1 tsp salt (soak + grind + ferment 8 hours). FOR SAMBAR: Refer to Recipe F007 (Onam Sambar)
preparation: STEP 1 (IDLI BATTER — DAY BEFORE): Same as dosa batter but slightly thicker. Grind coarser. Ferment overnight. STEP 2: Grease idli plates. Fill with batter (about 3/4 full). STEP 3: Steam in idli steamer for 12-15 minutes on medium heat. STEP 4: Insert a toothpick — should come out clean. Rest 5 minutes before demoulding. STEP 5: SAMBAR: Refer to Recipe F007. STEP 6: Serve hot idlis with sambar and coconut chutney.
tips: The classic South Indian breakfast. Fermentation quality determines softness of idlis.

name: Poha
ingredients: 2 cups thick poha (flattened rice), 1 onion (chopped), 1 potato (small cubes), ½ cup peanuts, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin, 10 curry leaves, 2 green chillies, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander, 2 tbsp grated coconut, sev for garnish
preparation: STEP 1: Rinse poha 2-3 times in a colander until softened. Do NOT soak. Sprinkle turmeric and salt. Mix gently. Set aside. STEP 2: Heat oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin, curry leaves, green chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 3: Add peanuts. Roast 1 minute until golden. STEP 4: Add potato cubes. Sauté 3 minutes until edges are golden. STEP 5: Add onion. Sauté 3 minutes until translucent. STEP 6: Add sugar. STEP 7: Add poha. Mix gently. Cover and cook on low heat 3 minutes. STEP 8: Turn off heat. Add lemon juice, coriander, and grated coconut. STEP 9: Serve topped with sev.
tips: The most popular Indian breakfast. Rinsing (not soaking) is crucial — otherwise poha becomes mushy.

name: Curd Rice
ingredients: 1 cup cooked rice, 2 cups thick curd (whisked), 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp urad dal, 1 tsp chana dal, 8 curry leaves, 2 green chillies (chopped), 1 dry red chilli, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 1 inch ginger (grated), 1 tbsp coriander, ¼ cup pomegranate seeds (optional)
preparation: STEP 1: In a bowl, mash cooked rice while warm to a slightly creamy consistency. Cool completely. STEP 2: Add curd and salt. Mix. STEP 3: Heat ghee in a small pan. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. STEP 4: Add urad dal and chana dal. Roast until golden. STEP 5: Add curry leaves, green chillies, dry red chilli, asafoetida, and grated ginger. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 6: Pour tempering over curd rice. Mix gently. STEP 7: Garnish with coriander and pomegranate seeds. Serve chilled or at room temperature.
tips: The ultimate comfort food for hot weather. Popular in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Cools the body.

name: Aloo Paratha
ingredients: FOR DOUGH: 2 cups whole wheat flour, 1 cup water, ½ tsp salt, 1 tsp oil. FOR FILLING: 4 boiled potatoes (mashed), 1 green chilli (chopped), 1 tbsp coriander, ½ tsp cumin powder, ½ tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp amchur, ½ tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp grated ginger, ghee for cooking
preparation: STEP 1: Prepare soft dough by kneading flour, water, salt, and oil. Rest 15 minutes. STEP 2: In a bowl, combine mashed potato, green chilli, coriander, cumin powder, red chilli powder, amchur, garam masala, salt, and ginger. Mix well. Do NOT add water. STEP 3: Divide dough into 8 balls. Divide filling into 8 balls (slightly smaller). STEP 4: Roll a dough ball into a small circle. Place filling in center. Bring edges together, sealing on top. STEP 5: Roll gently into a 6-inch paratha, using minimal flour. Do not press too hard or filling will burst. STEP 6: Heat tawa on medium heat. Place paratha. STEP 7: Cook 1 minute. Flip. Apply ½ tsp ghee. Cook 1 minute. Flip. Apply ghee on other side. STEP 8: Cook until brown spots appear on both sides. STEP 9: Serve hot with curd, butter, and pickle.
tips: The North Indian breakfast staple. Sealing edges well is key — otherwise potato bursts out.

name: Vegetable Pulao
ingredients: 1½ cups basmati rice (soaked 20 min), 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas, cauliflower), 1 onion (sliced), 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, whole spices (2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 inch cinnamon, 1 star anise), 1 tsp salt, 3 cups water, 2 tbsp coriander, 10 cashews
preparation: STEP 1: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 2: Add whole spices. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 3: Add cashews. Roast 30 seconds. STEP 4: Add sliced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until translucent. STEP 5: Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 6: Add mixed vegetables. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 7: Add drained rice. Mix gently. STEP 8: Add 3 cups water and salt. Stir. STEP 9: Close cooker. 2 whistles on medium heat. STEP 10: Natural pressure release. Fluff with fork. Garnish with coriander. Serve with raita.
tips: A quick one-pot meal. Do not over-stir rice — grains break. Use ghee for authentic flavour.

name: Mixed Vegetable Sabzi
ingredients: 3 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, cauliflower, peas, potato, capsicum — chopped), 1 onion (chopped), 2 tomatoes (chopped), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Heat oil. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 2: Add onion. Sauté 3 minutes. STEP 3: Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 4: Add tomatoes. Cook 4 minutes until soft. STEP 5: Add all spices (except garam masala). Sauté 1 minute. STEP 6: Add mixed vegetables. Mix well. STEP 7: Add ½ cup water. Cover and cook on low heat 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender. STEP 8: Sprinkle garam masala. Garnish with coriander. Serve with roti.
tips: A weekday staple. Use whatever vegetables are in season and in the fridge.

name: Bhindi Masala
ingredients: 500g bhindi (okra — washed, dried, sliced), 2 onions (sliced), 2 tomatoes (chopped), 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 3 tbsp oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp amchur, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Wash bhindi thoroughly. Dry COMPLETELY with a cloth (moisture = sticky bhindi). Slice into 1-inch pieces. STEP 2: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a kadai. Add bhindi. Sauté on high heat 8-10 minutes until crisp and non-sticky. Remove and set aside. STEP 3: In the same pan, add remaining oil. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 4: Add onion. Sauté 4 minutes. STEP 5: Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 6: Add tomatoes. Cook 4 minutes. STEP 7: Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 8: Add cooked bhindi back. Toss gently. STEP 9: Add amchur. Cook 2 minutes. STEP 10: Garnish with coriander. Serve with roti.
tips: CRITICAL: Bhindi MUST be completely dry before cooking, else it becomes slimy. Cook on high heat.

name: Tomato Rasam
ingredients: 3 large tomatoes (chopped), 1 lemon-sized ball tamarind (soaked, extracted), ¼ cup toor dal (cooked, mashed — optional), 2 tsp rasam powder, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp jaggery, 4 cups water, FOR TEMPERING: 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin, 2 dry red chillies, 10 curry leaves, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 3 crushed garlic cloves (skip for Jain), 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Boil chopped tomatoes with 1 cup water for 5 minutes until soft. Blend to a puree. STEP 2: In a pot, combine tomato puree, tamarind extract, cooked dal (if using), rasam powder, turmeric, salt, jaggery, and 3 cups water. STEP 3: Bring to a boil on medium heat. STEP 4: Once foam starts forming on top (do NOT let it fully boil), reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes. STEP 5: TEMPERING: Heat ghee in a small pan. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin, dry red chillies, curry leaves, asafoetida, and crushed garlic. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 6: Pour over rasam. Garnish with coriander. Serve hot with rice or as a soup.
tips: Rasam should NEVER be boiled fully — it loses its flavour. The foam formation is the sign to reduce heat.

name: Mango Lassi
ingredients: 1 cup thick curd, 1 ripe mango (chopped) or ½ cup mango pulp, 3 tbsp sugar (adjust), ½ tsp cardamom powder, ¼ cup cold milk, few ice cubes, chopped pistachios for garnish
preparation: STEP 1: In a blender, add curd, mango, sugar, cardamom, and cold milk. STEP 2: Blend for 1 minute until smooth and frothy. STEP 3: Taste and adjust sweetness. STEP 4: Pour into glasses over ice cubes. STEP 5: Garnish with chopped pistachios. Serve immediately.
tips: The summer favourite. Use ripe alphonso or kesar mangoes for best flavour.

name: Ragi Roti
ingredients: 2 cups ragi (finger millet) flour, 1 medium onion (chopped fine — skip for Jain), 1 green chilli (chopped), 1 inch ginger (grated), 2 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin seeds, ½ tsp salt, hot water as needed, ghee for cooking
preparation: STEP 1: In a bowl, combine ragi flour, onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, cumin, and salt. STEP 2: Slowly add hot water (start with ½ cup). Knead into a soft dough. Rest 5 minutes. STEP 3: Divide into 8 balls. Take one ball. Pat directly on a greased banana leaf, plastic sheet, or wet cloth into a 5-inch round (like thumb-flattening). STEP 4: Heat tawa on medium heat. Transfer roti carefully. Make small holes with finger (helps cooking). STEP 5: Cook 1 minute. Drizzle ½ tsp ghee. Flip. Cook 1 minute on other side. STEP 6: Serve hot with chutney or dal.
tips: Ragi is one of the LOWEST GI grains — excellent for diabetics. Rich in calcium and iron.

name: Methi Thepla (Diabetic)
ingredients: Refer to Recipe J007 with modification: substitute jaggery with 1 tsp stevia
preparation: Refer to Recipe J007 but skip jaggery entirely, or replace with stevia (½ tsp). Methi (fenugreek) actively LOWERS blood sugar — excellent for diabetics.
tips: Methi is a natural blood-sugar regulator. Thepla stays fresh 2-3 days — great meal-prep option.

name: Moong Dal Chilla
ingredients: 1 cup yellow moong dal (soaked 4 hours), 1 inch ginger, 2 green chillies, ¼ cup coriander, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp black pepper, ½ tsp cumin, ¼ cup water (as needed), oil for cooking, optional filling: paneer or vegetables
preparation: STEP 1: Drain soaked moong dal. STEP 2: In a blender, add moong dal, ginger, green chillies, coriander, salt, black pepper, and cumin. Blend to a smooth batter (like dosa consistency). Add water only if needed. STEP 3: Heat a non-stick tawa on medium heat. Grease with oil. STEP 4: Pour a ladleful of batter. Spread in a circle. STEP 5: Cook 2 minutes until edges lift. Drizzle ½ tsp oil around. Flip. STEP 6: Cook 1 minute. Add optional filling (grated paneer or sautéed vegetables). Fold. Serve hot with green chutney.
tips: PROTEIN + FIBRE = perfect diabetic breakfast. Very filling.

name: Cauliflower Rice Pulao
ingredients: 1 medium cauliflower (grated to rice-sized), 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 4 cardamom, 2 cloves, 1 bay leaf, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste (skip for Jain), 1 green chilli, ½ cup mixed vegetables (peas, carrot), 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp garam masala, 10 cashews, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Grate cauliflower into rice-sized granules (or pulse in food processor). Do NOT overprocess into paste. STEP 2: Heat ghee. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 3: Add cardamom, cloves, bay leaf. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 4: Add cashews. Roast 30 seconds. STEP 5: Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilli. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 6: Add mixed vegetables. Sauté 3 minutes. STEP 7: Add cauliflower rice. Toss well. STEP 8: Add salt. Cover and cook on low heat 5-7 minutes. STEP 9: Sprinkle garam masala and coriander. Serve hot.
tips: Almost ZERO carbs compared to regular rice. Perfect for strict diabetic control. Tastes similar to biryani.

name: Karela Sabzi
ingredients: 500g bitter gourd (karela — sliced, salted 20 min to reduce bitterness), 2 onions (sliced), 3 tomatoes (chopped), 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste (skip for Jain), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp amchur, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp jaggery (skip for strict diabetic)
preparation: STEP 1: Peel karela lightly. Slice into thin rounds. Sprinkle 1 tbsp salt. Rest 20 minutes. STEP 2: Squeeze karela thoroughly to remove bitter juices. Rinse well. STEP 3: Heat oil in a kadai. Add karela. Sauté on high heat 5-7 minutes until edges crisp. Remove and set aside. STEP 4: In the same pan, add cumin, onion. Sauté 4 minutes. STEP 5: Add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes. STEP 6: Add all spices (except amchur). Sauté 1 minute. STEP 7: Return karela to pan. Mix. Cook 3 minutes. STEP 8: Add amchur. Turn off. Serve with roti.
tips: Karela is one of the BEST natural blood-sugar regulators. The salting step removes bitterness while retaining medicinal benefits.

name: Brown Rice Khichdi
ingredients: 1 cup brown rice (soaked 30 min), ½ cup moong dal, ½ cup mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas), 5 cups water, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 1 inch ginger (grated), 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Wash and drain brown rice and moong dal. STEP 2: In a pressure cooker, add rice, dal, vegetables, turmeric, salt, and water. STEP 3: Pressure cook 5 whistles on medium heat (brown rice needs longer cooking). STEP 4: Let pressure release naturally. Open. Whisk lightly for creamy texture. STEP 5: TEMPERING: Heat ghee. Add cumin, asafoetida, grated ginger. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 6: Pour over khichdi. Garnish with coriander. Serve with curd or pickle.
tips: Brown rice + moong dal = complete protein + fibre. Much lower GI than white rice khichdi.

name: Palak Soup (Diabetic)
ingredients: 2 bunches spinach (blanched, chopped), 1 onion (chopped), 2 garlic cloves (skip for Jain), 1 tsp cumin, ½ inch ginger, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp salt, 3 cups vegetable stock or water, 1 tbsp cream (optional)
preparation: STEP 1: Blanch spinach 2 minutes, ice water shock. STEP 2: Heat olive oil. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 3: Add onion, garlic, ginger. Sauté 3 minutes. STEP 4: Add blanched spinach and stock. Simmer 5 minutes. STEP 5: Blend to a smooth soup. Return to pan. STEP 6: Add salt, black pepper. Simmer 2 minutes. STEP 7: Optional: swirl in 1 tbsp cream. Serve hot with a slice of multigrain toast.
tips: Very low calorie, nutrient-dense. Perfect diabetic dinner starter.

name: Tandoori Paneer Tikka
ingredients: 400g paneer (cubed), 1 cup thick curd (hung 30 min in muslin), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (skip for Jain), 2 tbsp tandoori masala, 1 tsp red chilli powder (Kashmiri), 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp mustard oil, 1 tbsp gram flour (besan) — roasted, capsicum + tomato + onion cubes for skewering, oil for grilling
preparation: STEP 1 (MARINADE): In a bowl, combine hung curd, ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala, red chilli powder, turmeric, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, mustard oil, and roasted besan. Whisk smooth. STEP 2: Add paneer cubes, capsicum, tomato, and onion. Toss gently to coat. STEP 3: Cover and refrigerate 45 minutes to 1 hour. STEP 4: Skewer alternating paneer, capsicum, tomato, onion cubes. STEP 5: Grill on a hot pan or oven at 220°C for 10-12 minutes, turning halfway, until edges are charred. STEP 6: Serve hot with mint chutney and onion rings.
tips: Grilled, no deep-frying = diabetic-friendly. Paneer is high protein, low carb.

name: Sprouts Salad
ingredients: 2 cups mixed sprouts (moong, chana, matki), 1 cucumber (chopped), 1 tomato (chopped), 1 small onion (chopped — skip for Jain), 1 green chilli (chopped), 2 tbsp coriander, 2 tbsp mint (chopped), 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp chaat masala, ½ tsp black pepper, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp olive oil (optional)
preparation: STEP 1: If sprouts are hard, steam briefly for 3-4 minutes to soften. Cool. STEP 2: In a large bowl, combine sprouts, cucumber, tomato, onion, green chilli, coriander, and mint. STEP 3: Add roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, black pepper, and salt. STEP 4: Drizzle lemon juice and olive oil. Toss well. STEP 5: Serve immediately.
tips: PROTEIN + FIBRE + LOW CARB = ideal diabetic meal. Very filling. Can add pomegranate for antioxidants.

name: Baked Kachori (Diabetic)
ingredients: FOR DOUGH: 1 cup whole wheat flour + ½ cup oats flour, 2 tbsp oil, ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp ajwain, water. FOR FILLING: 1 cup moong dal (soaked, coarsely ground), 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp fennel seeds (crushed), ¼ tsp asafoetida, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp amchur, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp oil for brushing
preparation: STEP 1 (DOUGH): Combine flours, oil, salt, ajwain. Rub with fingers. Add water gradually. Knead into a stiff dough. Rest 20 minutes. STEP 2 (FILLING): Heat 2 tbsp oil. Add cumin, fennel, asafoetida. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 3: Add ground moong dal. Sauté 5 minutes until fragrant and dry. STEP 4: Add all spices. Cook 2 minutes. Cool. STEP 5 (ASSEMBLY): Divide dough into 12 balls. Flatten each. Place 1 tbsp filling. Seal into a ball. Flatten gently into a thick disc. STEP 6 (BAKE): Preheat oven to 200°C. Place kachoris on a lined baking tray. Brush with oil. STEP 7: Bake 20-25 minutes until golden and crisp. STEP 8: Serve with mint-coriander chutney.
tips: Traditional kachoris are deep-fried. Baking cuts calories by 60% while keeping the taste. Add oats flour for extra fibre.
